readout_other: PCASL cerebral blood flow; resting-state fMRI within-region functional connectivity; MRS (GABA, glutamate, Glx)
direction_notes: Active tb-TUS reduced M1 cerebral blood flow and within-region functional connectivity relative to sham; no significant change in GABA, glutamate or Glx.

exposures.label: Theta-burst TUS to left M1 (active) vs left ventricle (sham)

timing.protocol_description: Theta-burst TUS (bursts of pulses repeated at a theta frequency, typically around 5 Hz) to the left M1, individually targeted with neuronavigation and acoustic simulation; sham aimed at the left ventricle. Sonication parameters are in supplemental Table S1, not in the main text.

source_quotes.n_subjects: 17 healthy subjects (nine females) aged 22–39 years (mean = 27.06, SD = 4.47) were included in the current study.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Theta-burst stimulation was delivered using the four-element NeuroFUS PRO - CTX-500 transducer (500 kHz; Brainbox Ltd., Cardiff, UK).
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: Theta-burst stimulation was delivered using the four-element NeuroFUS PRO - CTX-500 transducer (500 kHz; Brainbox Ltd., Cardiff, UK).
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: Theta-burst stimulation was delivered using the four-element NeuroFUS PRO - CTX-500 transducer (500 kHz; Brainbox Ltd., Cardiff, UK).
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.ispta_w_cm2: Acoustic simulations were iteratively refined until the active tb-TUS intracranial spatial peak temporal average intensity (ISPTA), a common measure of how much ultrasound energy is being delivered to the brain tissue, fell within 620–720 mW/cm².
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Each participant received both sham and active theta-burst TUS stimulation in a randomized order over the course of three days.

flags.reason: Stated as 620-720 mW/cm2; recorded as [0.62, 0.72] W/cm2 (unit conversion only). It is the simulated intracranial ISPTA target window for the active condition.
Pulse, PRF, duty cycle and duration are in supplemental Table S1 only.
Sham is real ultrasound focused in the left ventricle with a deeper focus and lower ISPTA, hence active_control_site.
Active and sham sessions over three days; number of stimulation sessions not stated explicitly.
Transducer position and orientation kept identical to avoid differential auditory confounds; no masking sound reported.
